subject: Post-call: Performance & SLO qualification (VPC/private)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Leah Turner <leah.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Performance & SLO qualification (VPC/private)

Hi Leah —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the follow-up items so we can scope the Private/VPC performance qualification correctly. High-level notes:

- Primary use-case: real-time assistant for internal tooling (short responses, many concurrent users).
- Streaming required for token-by-token updates for the UI.
- We discussed routing through a customer VPC (VPC peering / Direct Connect) and potential on-prem option later.

Action items / info we need from ACME to size and validate SLOs:
1) Latency targets (end-to-end user-perceived): p50 / p95 targets for typical generation (please include target token counts if they differ).
2) Throughput & concurrency: expected sustained QPS, expected peak QPS, and target concurrent inferences (number of simultaneous sessions).
3) Typical request sizes & avg response token length (gives us token/sec estimates).
4) Streaming requirements: target token-to-token latency and acceptable first-byte latency.
5) Network path: VPC peering vs Direct Connect vs VPN, whether egress goes through a NAT/Gateway, and whether there are internal firewalls/load balancers in the path.
6) IP ranges, expected test CIDR ranges and any IP allowlist process.
7) Any egress cost or data residency constraints we should know about.
8) Key management requirements (KMS/HSM) and whether you need customer-managed keys.
9) Preferred maintenance windows and upgrade blackout windows.

Attachments: I’ve attached our Redwood SLO checklist (redwood_slo_checklist.pdf) and a sample network checklist.

Next steps:
- If you can share the answers above and your network diagram (or let us know a shared Drive link), we’ll schedule a technical deep-dive with Aditya to validate routing and run a small benchmark.
- Proposed times for the deep-dive: Mon Jun 22 or Tue Jun 23 (10:00–11:00 PT). Let me know what works.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate with Aditya to prep test harness and sample load profiles once we have your numbers.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood_slo_checklist.pdf
From: Leah Turner <leah.turner@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Max Chen <max.chen@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance & SLO qualification (VPC/private)

Hi Marissa —

Great summary, thanks. Answers below inline and attaching our current network diagram and security questionnaire.

1) Latency targets: our goal is user-perceived latency. For typical responses under 256 tokens: p50 = 50ms, p95 = 180ms (end-to-end from UI request to last token). For longer generation workloads we can accept higher tail latency but prefer to understand tradeoffs.

2) Throughput & concurrency: expected sustained QPS around 60 req/s. Peak observed during busy periods ~140–160 req/s. Concurrent inferences we need to support ~400 concurrent sessions (many short synchronous calls).

3) Typical payload: average prompt ~120 tokens, avg response ~80–120 tokens. Spike cases up to 512 tokens.

4) Streaming: yes — token-by-token updates are required. Token-to-token latency target ~250ms or less for a smooth UI. First-byte latency should be <=200ms ideally.

5) Network path: we prefer AWS Direct Connect to our VPC (us-west-2). Egress for model requests currently goes through a NAT gateway; however we can allow specific peering if needed. There is a firewall (transit gateway + internal NLB) that could add a small amount of overhead (~5–15ms typical).

6) IP ranges / allowlist: attaching acme_network_diagram.pdf and acme_security_questionnaire.pdf. We can provide specific test CIDRs — will coordinate with Max.

7) Egress / residency: all traffic will originate from our us-west-2 VPC; no EU data residency requirements for this workload. Egress cost is a consideration but manageable.

8) KMS: we would like customer-managed keys for production.

9) Maintenance windows: weekday evenings (20:00–23:00 PT) are preferred for any disruptive testing.

Let us know how you measure latency (edge-to-model vs Redwood-internal). Also happy to schedule the deep-dive — Mon Jun 22 10:00 PT works for us.

Thanks,
Leah
Director, Developer Platforms | ACME Corp
leah.turner@acme.com
Attachments: acme_network_diagram.pdf, acme_security_questionnaire.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance & SLO qualification (VPC/private)

Leah —

Appreciate the details and the attachments. Quick notes and next steps:

- Measurement: for the qualification run we propose measuring both (a) edge-to-model (user-perceived) and (b) Redwood-runtime-only (after ingress) so we can isolate network overhead vs model inference time. We'll share the test harness results with both metrics.

- Based on your numbers (p95 180ms target, streaming token-to-token ~250ms, 400 concurrent sessions), our quick sizing suggests a dedicated pool with X GPUs (we'll send an exact recommendation after Aditya's deep-dive).

- Action: Aditya will run a network RTT test and small-scale benchmark from your VPC once you provide a test CIDR / allowlist. Aditya — can you confirm availability Mon Jun 22 10:00 PT for the deep-dive and if you need any specific firewall exceptions or ephemeral ports opened?

- Can you share the NAT/egress IPs or confirm if you prefer us to connect via Direct Connect peering? If Direct Connect, please share the peering contact and proposed ASNs.

- KMS: we support CMKs — we'll include KMS integration in the production design and document key rotation options.

Attachments: sample_ip_list.csv (attached) — please add your test CIDR and return.

Thanks — looping in Aditya to take the technical lead. Looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
